reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily comments on Bitcoin and broader market conditions using price charts and qualified discussion rather than promising guaranteed results. It includes ordinary promotions for exchange sign-ups, bonuses, and strategy links, but does not establish deceptive terms or a fabricated service. The video warns that trading is very risky and is not financial advice.

opening.argument: Judge, the bonus is tied to a concrete participation path. The description puts exchange registration, a bonus claim, and links to the speaker's bots in one numbered sequence. It also advertises a 50 USDT campaign, while the speaker directs viewers who want to join his next trade to a link with a deposit bonus. That is more than a passing mention of an exchange: the promised benefit gives viewers a reason to follow the links and enter the trading flow. The record does not establish the bonus terms or what happens after a viewer follows those links.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites a conditional Bitcoin trade, but that does not answer the separate bonus solicitation. Nor does quoting “Sign Up To Pionex” capture its placement immediately before “Claim Bonuses” and the bot links. A risk warning may qualify trading outcomes; it does not supply the missing terms for the advertised bonus or establish what the linked claim requires.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited text advertises bonuses and exchange links, but it does not say the bonus is free of conditions or show that its terms are false. The speaker explicitly warns that trading is very risky and limits his recommendation to experienced traders. The bonus language supports a finding of promotion, not by itself a deceptive reward scheme.

citations.quote: TOOBIT CAMPAIGN: 🔥50 USDT: https://bit.ly/4rDmWpg
Trading is VERY risky, and 80% of traders don't make money. Make sure that you understand these risks if you are a beginner. I only recommend crypto trading to already experienced traders!

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The speaker says his trading strategies are making “incredible gains,” then tells viewers to sign up, claim deposit bonuses, and open the same strategies with one click. The description presents links to his bots. The concern is not that every market forecast must be right; it is that an unverified gains claim sits beside an unusually direct path from exchange registration to copying his trades. A general warning about risk does not substantiate those gains or show how the linked bots perform for viewers.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes qualified price scenarios, but those qualifications concern Bitcoin's direction, not the asserted performance of the speaker's strategies. His phrase “in my opinion” qualifies his preference; it does not verify the “incredible gains” used to make the linked strategies attractive. The disclaimer warns of risk while leaving that particular performance claim unsupported.

citations.quote: my trading strategist are making incredible gains for everyday goes by

Nothing in this video is financial advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Incredible gains” is an unsupported performance assertion, but the cited material does not promise that viewers will achieve those gains or show a deceptive bot mechanism. The speaker describes possible trades conditionally and says he may not take one of them. He also explicitly warns that most traders do not make money. The combination warrants caution, but these excerpts do not establish a scam.

So that is a trade I'm potentially going to make. I will share that with you of course if I end up doing that.

opening.argument: Judge, the market discussion also serves as a route to the speaker's trading products. He moves from identifying trades he might make to inviting viewers to join his next trade, calling his own strategies the best way to trade, and directing them to exchange sign-up and bot links. The charts and geopolitical discussion may be genuine commentary, but they also give context and credibility to that invitation. Assess the video as a solicitation to use the speaker's linked strategies, not only as commentary on where Bitcoin may go.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The trading links are promotional, but promotion does not make the preceding analysis a pretext or establish deception. The speaker discusses competing long and short scenarios, says he is not convinced about immediate price action, and warns that trading is very risky. The prosecution identifies a path to his strategies, not evidence that the strategies or exchange offers are fabricated.
